findings.criterion: 2 and 3 — scanned-pass verification and camera check-in correctness
findings.issue: LiveCamera may report a QR and a plate from the same running camera while usePass is awaiting /v1/passes/lookup. onPlate immediately navigates to confirm, but pass lookup state is not represented in FlowState and Confirm is disabled only for busy or an empty plate. The attendant can therefore submit while flow.pass is still null, taking the ordinary /v1/sessions branch; the later valid lookup cannot retroactively redeem or associate the pass. LiveCamera also reports a different QR immediately, and usePass has no request sequence/abort guard, so an older lookup that resolves last can overwrite a newer accepted pass.
findings.consequence: A guest presenting a valid pass can be checked in as an ordinary paid stay with the pass left active, or the wrong guest pass can be redeemed after two scans resolve out of order.
findings.correction: Model pass validation as a sequenced pending operation shared by capture and confirm: pause/guard camera transitions when a QR is detected, ignore stale lookup responses, and disable confirmation until the current lookup settles. Add a deferred component/flow regression that triggers QR then plate, attempts confirmation before lookup resolution, and proves only /v1/passes/redeem is possible after success; also resolve two QR lookups out of order and prove the newest scan wins.

findings.criterion: 1 — resident can actually share a scannable QR pass
findings.issue: The source now supplies a fragment guest URL and a public QR page, but the recorded test only calls pure URL/parser helpers. The implementer explicitly did not execute a rendered/component/browser path, so no evidence establishes that the resident button invokes the file-share, text-share, or download/clipboard branch, that a directly opened shared URL renders in the deployed SPA, or that its rendered QR reaches lookup/redeem.
findings.consequence: The required user-facing Share affordance remains unverified across its reachable browser capability branches.
findings.correction: Add and record a rendered/browser test for file-capable Web Share, text-only Web Share, and no-Share fallbacks; inspect the actual shared/copied artifact, open the guest URL, decode/scan the rendered QR, and complete server lookup/redeem. Record browser, viewport, and results.

findings.criterion: 2 plus accessibility — pass prepopulate, focus, edit, and submit in context
findings.issue: The new tests exercise pure state patches only. No rendered execution enters or scans a signed hinted pass, observes focus on the accepted banner and the visible editable plate, edits/removes/replaces it, submits redemption, and verifies the persisted pass/plate association.
findings.consequence: The acceptance-critical prepopulate/verify/submit workflow and its keyboard/screen-reader transition are still not established in the actual UI.
findings.correction: Add and record a component/browser integration test covering signed hinted-pass acceptance, banner focus/live announcement, visible plate editing, removal/replacement, redemption, and persisted association; include the pending-lookup race correction above.

findings.criterion: 3 and 4 — camera scanning fills check-in and checkout plate fields
findings.issue: The implementer explicitly did not run the fake-camera story. The existing story covers only check-in, and there is still no checkout fake-camera story; pure ALPR tests do not execute getUserMedia through the React callbacks and controlled fields.
findings.consequence: Actual camera-to-field behavior for both required workflows remains unverified in context.
findings.correction: Run and record the mobile fake-camera check-in story, add/run a checkout story that opens a session, scans its plate, asserts the checkout field value and correct review match without manual entry, and record browser, viewport, fixture/model, and result.

findings.criterion: 5 — configurable policy UI and configured 12-hour amount/message
findings.issue: The green API suite establishes the MXN/USD seeds, PATCH behavior, the default $5,000 overstay messages, and a custom $25 reminder, but it never executes a 12-hour overstay after a non-default policy value. The policy editor has also not been rendered or exercised: the unrun guest-pass E2E only reads the default and does not edit, save, and reload it.
findings.consequence: Execution evidence does not yet prove that an administrator can persist the configurable amount in the UI or that all guest/host/supervisor 12-hour notices use the changed currency-formatted value rather than the default.
findings.correction: Extend the API test to trigger overstay after setting a non-default amount and assert that guest, host, and supervisor messages contain that formatted amount plus the move-vehicle instruction while 10h/11h behavior stays unchanged. Add/run a browser test that edits the overstay field, saves, reloads, and observes the persisted value.

findings.criterion: 6 and 7 plus mobile/responsive authorization — Admin CRUD and Super Admin cross-property operations
findings.issue: The relevant browser stories were again explicitly not run. They remain desktop-only; the Super Admin story switches property but performs no edit/delete there, and no rendered test proves a regular administrator cannot read or mutate the second property.
findings.consequence: The user-facing, mobile-responsive CRUD workflows and cross-property role boundary required by criteria 6 and 7 remain unverified.
findings.correction: Run and record the existing stories, extend representative person/site/unit/slot CRUD to a narrow mobile viewport, perform edit/delete after a Super Admin switches to a second property, and assert a regular administrator cannot read or mutate that property.
